Comment “Guide” and I’ll send you the prompts + a detailed breakdown.

I’ve been experimenting a lot of Artificial Intelligence in video, specifically for visual effects purposes and 3d workflows. Most of the issues I run into stem from the generations simply looking bad,  nonsensical or inaccurate. Good prompting helps, but it’s not perfect. Instead of fighting it, I’ve found leaning into that chaos breeds this super interesting style I’ve recently grown pretty fond of. 

Since the output of these prompts and generations are still generally random, I treat them as shots I’d receive on any other editing project: I don’t necessarily know what I’m working with until I get them. Which to me is kinda fun.

There’s 3 major steps from here:

1. Recut Everything. Throw everything into a timeline and cutaway the bad, build a storyline and splice things in a way that makes thematic sense. 

2. Reshoot Everything. You’re stupid dealing with AI, and unless you have a billion dollars to spend on generations, you’re exporting between 480-1080p. Because that quality isn’t sharp and often comes with artifacts, what I like to do is reshoot my monitors with a macro diopter to introduce new textures to the shot and hide the imperfections.

3. Cut Again: you’ll be left with shots that weren’t framed exactly like the originals. So at this point I always run a final pass over and make sure things cut together before I get into the sound design and add final touches in after effects.

The @higgsfield.ai plugin in DaVinci has really helped speed up this whole process. Since I no longer need to leave the software to get some of the early legwork done.

Frames of the Dolomites
The older I get, the more I realize it’s never really about the destination. It’s about the people you get to experience it with. 
Shot on @djiglobal Osmo Pocket 3 

There are places that look beautiful in photos. And then there are the Dolomites, which somehow look even better in real life.

You spend hours hiking for a view that only lasts a few minutes. Somehow, that’s exactly what makes it worth it.

Standing in front of mountains like these reminds you how small your problems actually are.

No notifications. No distractions. Just fresh air, good conversations, and endless peaks.

It’s funny how the places that make you feel the smallest often make you feel the most alive.

Maybe that’s why I keep coming back to the mountains. They don’t change who you are. They simply remind you of who you’ve been all along.

Over the past 5 years, I’ve had the privilege of exploring distant parts of our planet, and the honor to capture some of them through my camera. 

No AI.

Shot on @canonusa and @djiglobal 

Portrait of Eagle Hunter & Eagle — 2025, Kyrgyzstan 🇰🇬

A beautiful morning at Mont Saint-Michel — 2023, France 🇫🇷 

Volcanic ash extraction operation — 2022, Iceland 🇮🇸 

Paragliding over the Pharaohs — 2024, Egypt 🇪🇬 

After spotting an abandoned building’s balcony from the streets of Cairo, my friend Angelina and I planned to come here the next day to capture this photograph — 2024, Egypt 🇪🇬 

A light painting photograph I captured of myself with my friend Dino at Sarakiniko beach — 2023, Greece 🇬🇷 

My friend Anton standing in one of the worlds oldest and casts deserts — 2024, Namibia 🇳🇦 

I was onboard the Kinfish as it departed from Svalbard to go explore the Arctic sea and the North Pole — 2025, Norway 🇳🇴 

As we crossed the Sahara desert by foot, my brother stood on top of a dune at the perfect light — 2023, Morocco 🇲🇦 

A portrait I took of Sam as we crossed the Sarah desert onboard the Iron Ore train — 2026, Mauritania 🇲🇷 

“The Lonely Thinker” is a photograph I took that represents the self inside their own mind — 2023, Italy 🇮🇹 

One of my all time favorites, a light painting photograph of an Astronaut on top of the famous Solheimasandur Plane Wreck — 2022, Iceland 🇮🇸 

Beautiful morning in Rio as haze covered the city — 2024, Brazil 🇧🇷 

My mom and I spent 5 days crossing the desert of Lençóis Maranhenses, this is a photograph I took of our guide who was typically leading the way — 2022, Brazil 🇧🇷 

As my friend Dino and I explore the country, we randomly came across this magnificent beach — 2023, Greece 🇬🇷 

Near the southern town of M’hamid, the desert intertwines with these beautiful tall palm trees creating extremely unique landscapes — 2023, Morocco 🇲🇦 

Exploring the desert of Dubai by car — 2022, UAE 🇦🇪 

After spending a month with Almut, an artist who creates extremely unique and beautiful costumes, I was inspired. I dressed my friend up in one of those outfits and positioned him in front of a bus that was sitting on top

A lot of yall asked if I had a media pass/what camera I shot my video from @tomorrowland from but the truth is i was just a casual attendee and it was all on the tiny dji pocket 4p. It was the only camera I wanted to bring (or was even allowed to bring)  and it is pretty crazy how good the footage turned out for something so small! The DLOG2 captured some gorgeous scenes and the extra 3x lens really helped especially since I was pretty far back a lot of the time! Crazy how far cameras have come and how good hand held cameras are especially! #cinematic #djipocket #tomorrowland #travel
